what: Encode of the decoded twitter.cbor through ref_binding (handles; an identity for every node but integers and string keys), microseconds per document, 402806 bytes out. Arms in order: off (sharedrefs::off, main 2829e7d); on (sharedrefs::on, same header); v2 (after the count pass, only identities seen more than once go into numbers, and the write pass looks only there, and not at all when it is empty); v3 (v2 and seen.reserve(1 << 17)); v4 (v3 and seen in a std::pmr::unordered_map on a std::pmr::monotonic_buffer_resource).
why: The owner asked how much slower encode with shared references is, and to make it faster.
how: Google Benchmark, one binary per arm, each built twice (a, b). Runs of two arms each (off/on, on/v2, v2/v3, v3/v4), 3 rounds alternating, --benchmark_min_time=0.1s --benchmark_repetitions=3, random interleaving, GLIBC_TUNABLES trim_threshold, mmap_threshold and top_pad high. Medians.
finding: off 263/265, on 1739/1766 (6.6 times off). v2 1561/1573 against on 1786/1793 (-12 percent). v3 1349/1367 against v2 1561/1573 (-13 percent). v4 1233/1236 against v3 1351/1352 (-9 percent). From on to v4: -31 percent; v4 is still 4.7 times off. The count pass, one hash insert per node, takes most of the rest. mruby-cbor uses the same algorithm (walk_count, a Hash from object id to count).

context.commit: mbedded-cbor main 2829e7d, arms v2 to v4 are patches on it
